# apple_subscription_offer_code_one_time_use_code_values (Data Source)

Reads the codes Apple generated for an `apple_subscription_offer_code_one_time_use_code` batch — the same file App Store Connect offers for download.

This is a separate, opt-in data source rather than an attribute of the batch on purpose: every code is a secret anyone can redeem, and a batch holds up to 25,000 of them. Declare it only in the configuration that distributes the codes.

~> **The codes land in Terraform state in plain text.** `csv` is marked sensitive, which keeps it out of plan and console output, not out of the state file. Use a state backend that is encrypted and access-controlled, and prefer handing the value straight to wherever the codes go (a secret store, a mail-merge file) over outputting it.

Apple says codes can take up to an hour to become redeemable after the batch is created.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Opt-in, and only in the configuration that hands the codes out: the CSV is
# sensitive in plans but sits in state in plain text, so keep that state in an
# encrypted, access-controlled backend.
data "apple_subscription_offer_code_one_time_use_code_values" "term_1" {
  one_time_use_code_id = "9912345601"
}

# Inspect the document once; split it with csvdecode() if it has a header row,
# or by line if it does not.
locals {
  term_1_lines = compact(split("\n", data.apple_subscription_offer_code_one_time_use_code_values.term_1.csv))
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `one_time_use_code_id` (String) The ID of the `apple_subscription_offer_code_one_time_use_code` batch.

### Read-Only

- `csv` (String, Sensitive) The codes as the CSV document Apple returns, unmodified — Apple's API specification gives its media type as `text/csv` but does not describe its columns, so the provider does not parse it. Inspect it once, then split it with `csvdecode()` (if it has a header row) or `split("\n", ...)`.
- `id` (String) The batch ID, repeated.
